bindings.uiDescription: Toggles in-overlay navigation: focus ring, search and options.

uninstallMenu.name: Uninstall from the game list
uninstallMenu.description: Adds Uninstall options to the right-click menu on game tiles (Steam uninstall, game uninstaller, or move folder to Recycle Bin).

autoUpdate.name: Install updates automatically
autoUpdate.description: Downloads and installs new versions without asking, once no game is running. AW Next restarts on its own and says so afterwards.

showTrophies.name: Trophies on the profile
showTrophies.description: Shows platinum, gold, silver and bronze trophies under your name. Platinum is a game at 100%; the others rank your achievements by how many players unlocked them.

rarityDisplay.name: Rarity badges
rarityDisplay.description: Rare achievements only: gold, silver or bronze for the rarest ones, nothing for the rest. All: every achievement gets a badge by its unlock rate, and a finished game gets the platinum, like PlayStation trophies.

goldBelow.name: Gold trophy below
goldBelow.description: With all achievements, those unlocked by fewer players than this rate get gold.

silverBelow.name: Silver trophy below
silverBelow.description: With all achievements, those under this rate get silver; the rest, or those with no known rate, get bronze.

thresholds.name: Rarity thresholds
thresholds.description: Default keeps 5%, 10% and 15% for rare achievements, and 20% and 50% for all achievements. Custom lets you change them.

rareGoldMax.name: Gold up to
rareGoldMax.description: For rare achievements, those unlocked by this share of players or fewer get gold.

rareSilverMax.name: Silver up to
rareSilverMax.description: For rare achievements, those up to this rate get silver. It always stays above gold and below the rare limit: moving one slider pushes the others.

rareMax.name: Rare up to
rareMax.description: Up to this rate an achievement is rare: it gets bronze, the rare notification and its sound. Above it, nothing marks it.

playButton.name: Show Play button
playButton.description: Show the Play button on game tiles. Turn it off if you launch your games from another program. The right-click Launch game entry stays available.

size.name: Tile size
size.description: Size of the game artwork in the library grid.

density.name: Space between tiles
density.description: Gap around each tile, horizontally and vertically. Set it to 0 for a grid with no gaps at all.

showTitle.name: Game name
showTitle.description: Show the game name under its artwork. The List and Details views always keep it.

showProgress.name: Progress bar
showProgress.description: Show the completion bar on each tile.

showEmptyProgress.name: "No achievements" label
showEmptyProgress.description: For a game Steam lists with no achievements: write "No achievements" on its tile, or leave it blank. The game stays in the library either way.

showSource.name: Platform icon
showSource.description: Show the small Steam, GOG, Epic or emulator badge on each tile.

showHealth.name: Game health dot
showHealth.description: Show the coloured dot that warns when a game is not being tracked. Game health stays reachable from the right-click menu.

playtime.name: Playtime
playtime.description: How the library writes a long playtime: in days and hours, or in hours only.

showAchievementButton.name: Achievements button
showAchievementButton.description: Show the trophy button on the artwork. Clicking the tile itself opens the achievements either way.

showConfigButton.name: Game settings button
showConfigButton.description: Show the tools button in the top right corner of the artwork. Game settings stay reachable from the right-click menu.

compact.name: Profile banner
compact.description: Compact puts your avatar, name and stats on one row, so more of the library fits. The arrow in the banner switches it too.

emulator.intro: Safe, automatic repair for supported Steam/GBE Fork games.

autoApply.name: Automatically fix newly detected games
autoApply.description: Runs the safe Steam/GBE Fork repair once for a newly detected game. Disabled by default.

autoApplyMode.name: What the automatic fix does
autoApplyMode.description: Repair rewrites the files the emulator reads for everything Game Health flags, and installs the emulator only when no supported one is there. Always apply re-installs the whole GBE Fork setup instead. Neither takes a game away from a crack that already works.

manageDlc.name: Manage DLC ownership
manageDlc.description: Writes configs.app.ini so the emulator reports every DLC as owned. Unrelated to achievements: leave it off to keep a game stock or to manage DLC yourself. Disabled by default.

stampIdentity.name: Write account name and language
stampIdentity.description: Stamps your account name and language into each game's configs.user.ini. Leave it off if you rely on the emulator's central configuration for a predictable name and user ID. Disabled by default.

steamSettings.name: steam_settings data
steamSettings.description: Simple uses AW Next’s own fetch (anonymous). Advanced runs generate_emu_config for depot/language coverage.

login.name: Data source (Advanced)
login.description: Anonymous mode already retrieves public DLC/depot data. Steam login is optional: it only adds private or hidden data (such as some depots, branches or languages).

steamless.name: Auto-unpack SteamStub DRM
steamless.description: Runs Steamless on the game exe before patching to strip Valve’s SteamStub DRM (original kept as .steamstub.bak). No-op when there’s no stub.

steamlessExp.name: Steamless experimental
steamlessExp.description: Realigns sections during unpack for better compatibility with heavily-protected EXEs. Only matters when auto-unpack is on.

crackFix.name: Auto-apply community fix (CrakFiles)
crackFix.description: On every fix, automatically downloads and applies a community fix from the CrakFiles list when the name matches with high confidence (pixeldrain links only; overwritten files are backed up). Off by default - enable it if you want AW to download and overwrite game files from a community source.

help.title: Help & tips
help.intro: Everything useful to know: finding your games, notifications, emulators, the overlay, the controller, themes and what to do when something is wrong.
help.noResults: No help topic matches your search.
quick: Let Smart Find look for your games in Settings > Folders, or add a folder yourself, then enable the matching source in Settings > Sources.
The Watchdog runs in the background. It must be running for live notifications and playtime.
Everything (settings, caches, logs, custom themes) lives in %APPDATA%\Achievement Watcher Next.

The Interface control at the top of Settings switches between Simple (the everyday tabs) and Advanced (adds Steam / GBE Fork, Ubisoft / Uplay R1/R2, Advanced and deeper options). Simple only hides controls, nothing is turned off.
Closing the main window keeps AW Next in the system tray, where tracking goes on. To quit, use the tray menu. Launch at startup and Close to System Tray are in Settings > General.
The search field at the top of Settings finds an option in every tab. The First-run guide in Settings > General reopens the setup.
library: Collections: right-click a game > Collections, tick one or choose New collection…. The collections button next to Show installed games only then filters the library, and the profile numbers follow.
Edit collection… in that button’s menu changes the name, colour, icon or picture, and deletes the collection. The games stay in your library.
The round button next to the completion rate opens Library stats: completion, unlocked and locked counts, playtime, trophies, platinum games, rarest achievements and one row per platform.
A selector between the search field and the + button switches between six library views. Settings > Appearance > Library tiles sets the tile size, the spacing and what each tile shows.
The + button adds a game no source finds: a title and an executable, with an optional platform and Steam AppID. Launches and playtime are tracked, without achievements.
Right-click a game > Game settings > Rename… changes the name shown for it. Achievements & playtime > Edit playtime… fixes its total (12.5 or 12h30).
sources: Steam, Epic Games and Xbox PC each offer None, Installed or Owned in Settings > Sources. Owned lists the whole library of a connected account, installed or not.
GOG Galaxy, Epic, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox PC and EA Desktop each have their own switch in Settings > Sources. EA Desktop only covers games outside EA’s managed folders.
Owned Steam games count as installed only when Steam’s registry confirms it.
Steam unlocks are read from the stats Steam keeps on this PC, so a private profile works. Connecting an account is optional: it adds games played on another PC and Steam Family games.

A game saved somewhere unusual: add its folder in Settings > Folders. Choose the folder that directly holds the saves, the AppID folders or the emulator configuration, or a library folder that holds many games.
RetroAchievements: switch the source on, enter your username and Web API key, then press Import library. Unlocks come from your account, so keep RetroAchievements on in the emulator.
In Simple mode a few rarely used source rows stay hidden while they are unused. They come back as soon as they matter, and Advanced always lists them all.

PlayStation trophies show their grade and the share of players who have them. The rates come from Exophase; connect a PlayStation account in Settings > Sources to get Sony's own figures for the games on that account.

With a PlayStation account connected, Import library brings your PlayStation games and trophies, refreshed every three days, and the field under it adds a game you do not own. A game from another store that also came out on PlayStation shows its real platinum, and in trophy mode its real grades and DLC groups.
notifications: Automatic is the default: the in-game popup when the game can show it, a Windows notification when it cannot, never both.

Settings > Notification holds Notification type (Automatic, Windows notification, In-game overlay or Both), the preset, sound, volume, position, scale and opacity. The Tests buttons fire a real popup.
Open a game’s tools button (top right of its tile) and go to its notification settings to give that one game its own preset, position, sound or scale.
Screenshot on unlock keeps a picture of the moment in Pictures\Achievement Watcher Next.
Rare achievement sound, 100% completion sound and Progress sound (Advanced mode) give those popups a sound of their own. Random picks a different sound each time, and you can import your own files.
Gold, silver and bronze mark rare unlocks. Settings > General > Rarity display switches to Trophy mode, which grades every achievement and shows platinum on finished games.
For counters, Progress milestones shows a popup only at 10, 25 or 50% steps. Right-click a game > Mute progress notifications silences one game without touching its unlocks.
Two more switches in Settings > Notification: Priority notifications lets unlocks through Do Not Disturb (Windows 11), and Steam client games adds AW Next’s popup for games Steam itself runs.
gameHealth: Click the tools button of a game (top right of its tile), or right-click it, to open Game health. It says whether the game is Ready, Needs attention or Not tracking.
The sentence under the state explains the cause in plain words. The checks below show which part is at fault: game files, executable, achievement data, emulator setup, live tracking or notifications.

Repair buttons only appear when AW Next can really fix that game, such as Locate the game, Rewrite the achievement data, Restore the emulator file or Watch this game. Each one says what it will change, keeps a backup and asks first.
Send a test notification fires a popup with that game’s own name and artwork, delivered the way it really would be.
Technical details holds the exact paths, counts and emulator codes: press Copy and paste it into a bug report. The coloured dot on a tile can be hidden in Settings > Appearance > Library tiles.
troubleshoot: If a game is missing: check its source in Settings > Sources, run Smart Find or Generate configs in Settings > Folders, add its folder by hand if needed, and try turning off Show installed games only.

If notifications don’t appear: read the Notifications row in the game’s Game health, then check Windows Do not disturb / Focus Assist. Priority notifications in Settings > Notification can let unlocks through.
Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics opens the logs and data folders, and Export logs (.zip) bundles the logs with your user name and keys masked. Attach it when reporting an issue.
Logs are appended, so a crash survives the next launch. Each run starts with a session marker and a [diag] block (versions, paths, displays): paste it into an issue.
A game stuck at 0%? That is normal until its first unlock is written. If AW Next matched the wrong Steam release, right-click the game > Set AppID manually….
Playtime not counted? Open the game’s tools button > Executable and pick the program that stays open while you play, not a launcher.
New achievements from a game update appear within 3 days, or right away with Settings > Advanced > Recheck achievement lists.
An app update keeps failing on the same file? Settings > Advanced > Clear caches only removes re-downloadable files, never your settings or saves.
steam: GBE / Goldberg saves are usually under %APPDATA%\GSE Saves or %APPDATA%\Goldberg SteamEmu Saves.
CODEX / RUNE saves often live under Public Documents\Steam\CODEX or Public Documents\Steam\RUNE.

TENOKE, UniverseLAN, SmartSteamEmu, ALI213, Hoodlum, CreamAPI and the Nemirtingas emulators are read from their own config or save folders. If a game is not found, add its folder in Settings > Folders.

Right-click a game > Emulator & tools > Apply emulator fix… installs GBE Fork, builds steam_settings (achievement list and icons) and writes steam_appid.txt when it is missing. Every replaced file is backed up first.
In Settings > Steam / GBE Fork, steam_settings data set to Simple uses AW Next’s own anonymous fetch and is fast. Advanced runs generate_emu_config for deeper Steam data and can take minutes.
Nothing is written into a game folder on its own: Automatically fix newly detected games, Manage DLC ownership and Write account name and language are all off by default.
Diagnose emulator in the same menu only reads and reports. Back up GBE/Goldberg setup and Restore latest GBE/Goldberg backup put a game back the way it was.
emulators: RPCS3 trophies are read from dev_hdd0\home\...\trophy near the RPCS3 install. A moved virtual disk is followed.
shadPS4 trophies are read from its game_data folder (the TROP XML files). You can add the emulator, its user folder or game_data itself.
Xenia progress is read from the Xbox profile files (.gpd) and follows the storage folders set in its config.
KytyPS5 trophies are read from its _Trophies folder, for the user the launcher runs the game as.

Xbox 360 games recompiled for PC and PS4 ports (Bloodborne, Uncharted, God of War III Remastered, MediEvil and others) are their own sources in Settings > Sources. If one does not show up, add its folder in Settings > Folders.

Each console can have its own popup preset and sound in Settings > Notification > Emulators (Advanced mode). Recompiled Xbox 360 games follow Xenia’s choice, PS4 ports follow shadPS4’s, and Same as main keeps the main settings.
controller: In Settings > Controller, turn on Control the in-game overlay with a controller (off by default), then Back + Start + LB opens the overlay in game.

Control the app with a controller (on by default) drives AW Next itself: D-pad or left stick move the focus, A opens a game, B goes back, X searches, Y or Start opens Settings, LB / RB switch settings tabs.
In the library, RT launches the selected game and LT opens its Game health.
In the overlay, LB + X toggles navigation: D-pad or left stick move the focus, A confirms, B cancels, X searches, Y opens the options.
Hold LB + RB to move the overlay with the left stick and scroll with the right stick.
If the game still reacts to your buttons, turn on Focus overlay when it opens or Send Escape to the game when opening with controller (both off by default).
Works with Xbox, PlayStation (DualShock 4 / DualSense) and Switch Pro controllers. Controller layout sets the button names shown, and each shortcut takes one to three buttons.
Pad not detected? Check it in Windows (joy.cpl) first, make sure the right switch is on, then try XInput in Controller backend.
overlay: Open it with the overlay hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+K by default) or Back + Start + LB on a controller while a supported game runs. The hotkey is set in Settings > General.
It lists the achievements of the running game: name, description, locked or unlocked, unlock date and progress. Drag it by its header.
A hidden achievement stays hidden until you click it (or press A on a controller), so nothing is spoiled.
The pills All, Unlocked, Locked and In progress filter the list. Click Achievement, Rarity, Date or Status to sort: ascending, descending, then back to normal. One column at a time.
Press / to focus the search, Esc to clear it or close the options panel.
The gear panel changes accent, density, icon size, zoom, opacity and visible rows. Use app theme follows the active theme, and Reset defaults undoes it all.
Every achievement with a known rate shows its rarity: gray for common, gold/silver/bronze for rare.
stream: Settings > Notification > OBS browser source (Advanced mode): Preview checks it in your browser and Copy link copies the address. In OBS, add a Browser source and paste it as the URL.

Any width and height work, the card scales to fill the box. A bigger source is sharper: give it about twice the preset’s own size (http://127.0.0.1:8082/obs/_config reports it) and place it at half size.
Add ?test=1 to the URL while you place the source. It shows a sample unlock every ten seconds; remove it once you are done.
The source draws the same popup as the in-game one, and stays empty between unlocks so it costs nothing while you stream.

More options after the address: ?scale=2 pins the zoom, ?duration=8000 sets how long each card stays, ?sound=1 plays the sound through the source, /obs/preset/Xbox/ uses one preset whatever the desktop uses.
It reads the local notification feed, so leave Local broadcast on in Settings > Notification > Integrations. It only works on this PC, and only one copy of AW Next can serve it.
souvenirs: Settings > Notification > Screenshot on unlock saves a picture a moment after the popup, notification included, in one subfolder per game. Open folder takes you there.
HDR screenshots (Automatic) corrects the colours when Windows HDR is on. Souvenirs capture the primary monitor, so play on it.

Video clip on unlock (off until you turn it on, further down Settings > Notification) keeps the last seconds of play in memory and saves an MP4 around each unlock. Nothing is written until an achievement unlocks.
Clip length (10 to 30 seconds), Format (H.264, HEVC or AV1), Resolution, Frame rate, Quality and Sound (Game only or Whole PC) can all be changed. H.264 plays everywhere.

The graphics card’s own encoder does the work, with well under 1% of the processor. Without a hardware H.264 encoder, Windows’ software encoder takes over at 1080p and 30 FPS at most. A very old game in exclusive fullscreen may record black frames.
shortcuts: Ctrl+Shift+K (default): toggle the in-game overlay. Change it in Settings > General.
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Arrows move the overlay; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+1-5 snap it to a preset position; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C toggles click-through.
In the overlay, / focuses the search and Esc clears it. In the preset designer, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo.
Ctrl+F focuses the Settings search and Esc clears it. F5 refreshes the library.
themes: Settings > Appearance has built-in themes and every one can be edited: window, top bar, panels, cards, settings, text, borders and accent each take a colour, a gradient or an image.
Save theme turns your edit into a theme of your own: keep the name to replace it, type another for a copy. Reset all puts back the theme you started from.
Drop a CSS theme into <userData>\themes and it appears in the theme dropdown.
Export theme… writes one .awtheme file (a built-in must be saved under your own name first). Import theme… previews it before it installs, and Delete theme removes an imported one.
Themes made by the community are in the theme gallery on the project website, and sending yours takes one file.
presets: A preset is the look of the in-game popup, chosen in Settings > Notification > Preset. It has no effect when Notification type is Windows notification.

Settings > Notification presets is a designer made of ordinary controls: pick a starting point or press Surprise me, watch the live preview (Card, Compare, Screen), then Create preset. Nothing is saved before that.
Customize a bundled preset changes only a few things (background, text colour, accent, border, glow, font, logo) and keeps following the bundled preset if it improves.
Edit a preset reopens one you designed. Export and Import move a preset as one .awpreset file, with its images, fonts and sound.
Import > SAN theme… reads a Steam Achievement Notifier theme (a .san file), and Import > From SAN on this PC brings in the themes SAN already uses. They keep their SAN look and sounds.
tips: Right-click a game tile to launch it, choose its executable, open folders and links, use emulator tools, or uninstall it when that menu is enabled.
Mark as manually unlocked (right-click an achievement) records an unlock no source can see.
Reset achievements… plays a game again from zero and backs up every file first. It works for emulated games, not for Steam, Epic or Xbox, whose unlocks live on your account.
Playtime is tracked while the game runs; Playtime tracking in Settings > Notification turns on the start and end notifications.
Forget this game… clears everything AW Next keeps about a game (saves are backed up first). Remove from list only hides it.
Game settings > Achievement language shows one game’s achievements and notifications in another language than the rest.
Settings > Advanced > Profile backup: Export profile… saves your settings, presets, themes, covers and playtime in one .awbackup file for a reinstall or a new PC. Sign-ins are not saved.

fixAll.name: Fix all detected games
fixAll.description: Run the matching Steam/GBE Fork or Ubisoft/Uplay R1/R2 repair on every compatible detected game with a known install folder.
fixAll.confirm: Apply the emulator fix to every detected game with a known install folder? Existing files are backed up before being overwritten.
fixAll.none: No detected game with a known install folder to fix.

diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.desc: Your version, plus the logs and data folder to share when you report a problem.
diag.goldbergDesc: Scan a game-library folder for Goldberg / GBE Fork installs and flag the ones missing their steam_settings/achievements.json schema. Use a game’s right-click menu (Diagnose / Repair) to fix one.
diag.profileBackupDesc: Save your settings, library choices, presets, themes, covers and backups to one file, then bring them back after a reinstall or on a new PC. Sign-ins are never saved.

mainSteam.title: Main Steam Account
mainSteam.name: Filter by user
mainSteam.description: Show only the Steam achievements of the chosen account. All accounts: no filter.

clearUpdateCache.name: Clear caches
clearUpdateCache.description: Deletes re-downloadable caches: update files, Steam/Ubisoft schema & icon cache, and downloaded emulator-fix tools. Never touches your settings, saves, backups, or manually placed files.

forceAchievementRecheck.name: Recheck achievement lists
forceAchievementRecheck.description: Checks Steam for achievements added by a game update since the last check. Runs automatically every 3 days; this forces it now.

disableAutoRefresh.name: Automatic achievement data updates
disableAutoRefresh.description: Keeps achievement data up to date: fills in blank descriptions and picks up achievements a game update added. Turn it off only if you maintain these files yourself. "Recheck achievement lists" above still works by hand.

onboarding.settingsHelp: Reopen the setup guide for profile, folders, sources, and notifications.
onboarding.welcomeCopy: Two quick choices to start. Everything can be changed later in Settings, and you can skip the rest of this guide at any time.
onboarding.languageHint: Games, metadata, achievements and Steam caches all load in this language. The first library load starts after this choice.
onboarding.overlayCopy: Press {hotkey} in a game to see its achievements over it.
onboarding.collectionsCopy: Group games into your own collections from a game's right-click menu.
onboarding.trophyCopy: Grade achievements gold, silver or bronze by rarity, or by their real PlayStation trophy when the game also came out there. Turn it on in Settings.
onboarding.clipsCopy: Keep a short clip around each unlock. Turn it on in Settings under Notifications.
onboarding.statsCopy: Under your profile, “See the detailed breakdown” shows your completion, playtime and progress per platform.
onboarding.healthCopy: A coloured dot on a game tells you whether its achievements are tracked. Its settings button explains what is wrong.
onboarding.profileCopy: Pick the name shown in the header and optionally set a local avatar.
onboarding.avatarHint: Optional. Stored locally on this PC.
onboarding.foldersCopy: AW Next looks for games on this PC and shows what it finds. Add a folder only if something is missing.
onboarding.detectSteamOff: Your Steam games stay hidden until Steam is switched on under Sources.
onboarding.settingsCopy: Pick a theme and how unlock alerts appear. Use Test notification to see one right now.
onboarding.readyCopy: AW Next now watches your games in the background and tells you when you unlock something.
onboarding.summaryNoGames: No games found yet. You can add folders later in Settings.
onboarding.summaryReopen: You can reopen this guide at any time from Settings > General.
onboarding.sourcesCopy: Every source installed on this PC is read automatically, so the defaults are fine. Sign in below only if you want more.
onboarding.sourcesCopySimple: The launchers and emulators on this PC are already read. Connect an account only if you want what it adds.
onboarding.accountsCopy: Sign in to read unlocks from a private Steam profile, add your Steam Family games, import your Xbox PC library, show your Epic progress, get PlayStation's own trophy rates and import your RetroAchievements games. You can skip this and connect later in Settings > Sources.
onboarding.raKeyPage: Where is my Web API key?
onboarding.sourcesEmulatorsCopy: Each one is read only when it is installed, so leaving them on costs nothing.
onboarding.sourceHint: Also lists your legitimate Steam games (public profile required).
onboarding.notificationsHint: Where unlocks appear. Automatic picks the overlay or a Windows notification for you.
onboarding.playtimeHint: Automatically tracks playtime for detected games.
onboarding.autoFixHint: Applies the matching GBE Fork or Uplay R1/R2 repair to newly detected emulated games.
onboarding.hiddenHint: Reveals hidden achievement names and descriptions before you unlock them.
onboarding.mergeHint: Combines the same game found in several sources into a single tile.
onboarding.invalidFolder: That folder does not look like a supported achievement folder. Expected: GSE Saves / Goldberg SteamEmu Saves, CODEX/RUNE saves, AppID subfolders (e.g. 1091500), or a game folder with steam_settings or an emulator .ini.
onboarding.modeCopy: Both track achievements exactly the same way. This only decides how much of AW Next is on screen.
onboarding.modeSimpleCopy: A streamlined interface built around what you use every day: your library, notifications, appearance and sources.
onboarding.modeAdvancedCopy: The complete AW Next: emulator runtime setup, diagnostics, repair tools and experimental options.
onboarding.modeHint: Nothing is switched off either way - Simple shows less, and you can change this at any time in Settings.
onboarding.modeRequired: Choose Simple or Advanced to continue.

dialogs.preset-layer-fixed: {presets} draw their card with their own code, so they cannot be customized here. You can still use them as they are.
dialogs.preset-layer-named: It will be saved as a new preset, "{name}"; change the Name to call it something else.
dialogs.preset-layer-start-hidden: "{start}" is hidden while you customize a preset. Choose "{none}" to get it back.
dialogs.preset-play-popup: This preset draws its card with code of its own, so it plays in a real popup, on screen.
dialogs.preset-play-reduced: Windows is set to show fewer animations, so the preview stays still. Turn "Animation effects" back on in Windows settings to see them.

watchdog.testDescription: This is a test notification from AW Next.

startup.description: Starts AW Next automatically when you log in to your desktop session, hidden in the tray.

uninstallMenu.description: Adds Uninstall options to the right-click menu on game tiles (Steam uninstall, game uninstaller, or move folder to Trash).

priority.description: Give the overlay keyboard focus when it opens, so games that pause on focus loss do. AW Next does not take the controller away from the game, so the game may still see the buttons.

steamless.description: Runs Steamless on the game exe before patching to strip Valve’s SteamStub DRM (original kept as .steamstub.bak). No-op when there’s no stub. Needs Mono (mono-complete on Debian and Ubuntu).

apiCheckBypass.description: Off by default. Drops SteamAutoCrack’s bypass proxy (winmm.dll) + a redirect config so games that re-check the original steam_api/exe after the swap still launch and unlock. Downloads the proxy from its official release. Wine and Proton load the proxy only when the game’s launch options set WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winmm=n,b".

platinum.description: Fire a dedicated desktop notification when a game reaches 100% completion

mode.description: Automatic uses the in-game overlay when it can be shown and a desktop notification when it cannot. The other choices always use the one you pick.

customToastAudio.name: Desktop notification sound
customToastAudio.description: Specifies the sound to play when a desktop notification is displayed

urgent.description: Let achievement unlocks show while Do Not Disturb is active. They are sent as critical notifications, which most desktops let through.

useToast.name: Desktop notification
useToast.description: System notification shown by your desktop

option.souvenirDirHelp: One subfolder per game, files named "date - achievement". Default: ~/Pictures/Achievement Watcher Next. On Wayland the desktop asks once per session to share the screen.
option.clipDesc: While a game runs, its last seconds are kept and saved around each unlock, with the notification in the middle. On Wayland the desktop asks once to share the screen.
option.clipDirHelp: One subfolder per game, files named "date - achievement". Default: ~/Videos/Achievement Watcher Next.

folder.default: Folders checked automatically, in every Wine or Proton prefix and in your home folder

addInfo.2: ALI213.ini, valve.ini, hlm.ini, ds.ini, steam_api.ini, SteamConfig.ini, tenoke.ini or UniverseLAN.ini file is located. For RPCS3, select its configuration folder (~/.config/rpcs3) or its dev_hdd0 folder.

libraryInfo.0: Select a folder that holds many game install folders (e.g. ~/Games, or drive_c/Games inside a Wine prefix).

quick.2: Everything (settings, caches, logs, custom themes) lives in ~/.config/Achievement Watcher Next.

notifications.0: Automatic is the default: the in-game popup when the game can show it, a desktop notification when it cannot, never both.
notifications.3: Screenshot on unlock keeps a picture of the moment in ~/Pictures/Achievement Watcher Next.

troubleshoot.1: If notifications don’t appear: check that Do Not Disturb is off on your desktop and that its notification settings do not block AW Next.

sources.2: Owned Steam games count as installed only when Steam’s own files confirm it.

steam.0: GBE / Goldberg saves are usually under AppData/Roaming/GSE Saves inside the game’s Wine or Proton prefix, or under ~/.local/share/GSE Saves for a native Linux game.
steam.1: CODEX / RUNE saves often live under Public/Documents/Steam/CODEX or Public/Documents/Steam/RUNE inside the game’s Wine or Proton prefix.

emulators.0: RPCS3 trophies are read from dev_hdd0/home/.../trophy in RPCS3’s folder (~/.config/rpcs3).

themes.2: Drop a CSS theme into ~/.config/Achievement Watcher Next/themes and it appears in the theme dropdown.

onboarding.notificationsHint: Where unlocks appear. Automatic picks the overlay or a desktop notification for you.

dialogs.n-nno-uninstaller-was-found-in-this-fold: No uninstaller was found in this folder. The files will be moved to the Trash (recoverable).
dialogs.could-not-move-the-folder-to-the-recycle: Could not move the folder to the Trash.
dialogs.delete-permanently-detail: A permanent delete skips the Trash: the files cannot be restored.
dialogs.delete-recycle-bin-refused: The system refused to move this folder to the Trash. That happens when a file is still open, when the drive has no Trash (a removable or network drive), or when you cannot write to the folder.
dialogs.delete-blocked-by-permissions:
This file is not writable by your account: {file}
Only its owner or root can delete the folder.
